confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on two web searches. They are cross-checked against crowd-sourced cost-of-living aggregators such as Expatistan, which listed a cappuccino at about 84 EGP (about 1.63 USD) and a 500 ml beer at about 82 EGP. Other aggregators gave an inexpensive meal at about 4 USD and a mid-range dinner at about 14 USD per person. The sources disagree in places and some are out of date. Egypt's high inflation also makes current prices less reliable. The July 2026 window is an estimate rather than measured data. Beer is set a little above the neighbourhood-pub figure because alcohol is mostly served in licensed bars and hotels, where one source put a local beer at about 3.8 USD. I estimated the cocktail and wine anchors from their usual price ratio to beer in licensed venues. I did not find direct aggregated prices for them, so they are less certain. The mid-range meal for two is cut slightly below twice the per-person figure, because the definition excludes drinks. Accommodation anchors are my own estimates from general knowledge only, not from searches or listings. The FX figure is the 18 Nov 2026 RBA 4pm reading as reported in search results. I did not open the RBA page myself to confirm the number.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared Cairo with other low-cost North African and Middle Eastern capitals, such as Amman and Tunis, and adjusted for the weak Egyptian pound. I also allowed for alcohol costing more because of licensing.
